title.narrative: Green transition of shipping in developing countries

description.narrative: An accelerated just and equitable green transition of shipping in developing countries, with a specific focus on Africa, by building financial, technical and human capacities of developing countries. By addressing capacity barriers, the project seeks to create enabling environments that attract investment in green technologies and infrastructure, thereby fostering sustainable green growth and unlocking development opportunities. in developing countries.

actual.value: Significant progress has been achieved under Outcome 1 in 2025. Workshops held in Kenya, South Africa and Senegal helped reduce knowledge gaps related to the implementation of the 2023 IMO GHG Strategy in the African region, increased awareness of the importance of ratifying MARPOL Annex VI, encouraged concrete commitments to developing National Action Plans, promoted sustainable port development, prioritized seafarer training and green job opportunities, and strengthened national and sub-regional coordination among stakeholders. 2 Building on this, the Workshops further strengthened awareness of shipping decarbonization in Africa and supported progress in enhancing coordination between the maritime and energy sectors, increasing the participation of African Member States in IMO meetings, and advancing workforce development for the green transition. 3 IMO provided technical expertise in preparing the Workshop programmes, which also helped identify potential partners in the region, particularly among Francophone African countries that have been less engaged in GHG-related IMO discussions. Senegal announced its intention to ratify MARPOL Annex VI and requested IMO technical assistance for the development of its Maritime Single Window and National Action Plan, as well as capacity building for Port State Control Officers. 4 Participants of the Workshops expressed appreciation for the Voluntary Multi-Donor Trust Fund (VMDTF), which supports developing countries' participation in IMO GHG-related meetings, and for the GHG-SMART online core sessions, noting interest in further online training opportunities. Fifteen key declarations resulting from the Workshop in Senegal were submitted to the second extra-ordinary session of MEPC, which took place in October 2025,in document MEPC/ES.2/2/9 (Angola et al.).

title.narrative: Two green pilot project owners in developing countries have developed compre-hensive feasibility studies for zero or near-zero emissions pilot projects that are con-sidered finance-ready. This should enable them to make informed decisions about the next steps for implementing their pilot projects.

target.value:
Through the GreenVoyage2050 Pilot Accelerator opportunities for two pilot projects have been identified, and pilot owners have been selected, ideally focusing on Energy Efficiency Technology pilots.
Public-private partnerships developed to bring ac-tive private sector participation to support devel-opment of pilot projects.

actual.value: 1 GreenVoyage2050 has supported 2 developing countries (Indonesia and Turkiye) with the funding provided by Denmark to develop pilot feasibility studies: .1 Indonesia: The GreenVoyage2050 PCU is supporting a "Feasibility study for modification of an interisland ferry from conventional to hybrid propulsion, encompassing hydrogen fuel in combination with battery technology". The pilot focuses on assessing the feasibility of introducing a hybrid electric-hydrogen propulsion system for ferry operations on the Kupang Rote route. Through support provided by Houlder Ltd., GreenVoyage2050 is funding and coordinating a comprehensive feasibility study and associated design work covering techno-economic viability, policy and regulatory considerations, safety and environmental assessments, and stakeholder capacity-building. The study complements broader national efforts to explore hydrogen applications in the maritime sector, including related land-side hydrogen production and infrastructure assessments being supported by GIZ. Work is currently underway, with delivery of the study expected by Q3 2026. .2 Turkiye: The GreenVoyage2050 PCU is supporting a "Study exploring the potential for electrification of the ferry network servicing the Sea of Marmara" in Turkiye, implemented with technical support from Ricardo. The study is providing Turkiye with targeted technical guidance as it explores electrification and hybridization options for vessels operating in the Sea of Marmara, including analysis of vessel retrofitting requirements, shore-side charging infrastructure, and potential energy supply options. During the reporting period, substantial progress was made on data collection and technical assessments covering more than 50 RoRo and RoPax vessels and routes. Preliminary analysis identified several routes with strong potential for feasible electrification. As part of the project, stakeholder workshops and consultation meetings were held in Istanbul, bringing together ferry operators, ports, shipyards, electricity providers, academia, government representatives, and international financial institutions. The active participation of international financial institutions such as the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) has helped ensure that the identified case studies are aligned with future financing support and investment considerations. The study is expected to be finalized Q2 2026 and will support informing next steps towards pilot implementation and financing discussions

target.value:
One seafarer training programme has been developed to support the handling of zero or near-zero carbon fuels and technologies. It covered: 1) Overview of zero and near-zero carbon fuels and technologies, 2) Safety and handling procedures, 3) Technical operation and maintenance, 4) Regulatory compliance, and 5) Case studies and best practices

title.narrative: Two developing countries have developed National Action Plans (NAP) to address their shipping GHG-emissions. For each country, the plan has been endorsed by an inter-ministerial National Task Force (NTF).
Number of National Action Plans and written confirmation of endorsements from inter-ministerial National Task Forces.

target.value: Two inter-ministerial NAP development National Task Forces (NAP NTFs) have been established with relevant national policymakers to promote pro-gress, transparency, accountability, and consensus-building towards the development of National Ac-tion Plans (NAP). A NAP kick-off Roundtable has been facilitated to discuss the benefits and drivers for the develop-ment of a NAP in the country. The session also in-troduced the NAP Guide and shared experiences from countries that have developed and adopted NAPs. The event included participation from NAP NTF member and relevant maritime stakeholders.

actual.value:
Ghana: Has prepared a draft NAP in advance of joining the GreenVoyage2050 Programme. Support has been requested to refine this draft NAP, primarily focusing on undertaking a Baseline Assessment to support evidence-based decision making within the NAP. To undertake the Baseline Assessment and provide concrete policy recommendations, Ricardo AEA was contracted. A kickoff workshop was conducted in Q1 2025 by the GreenVoyage2050 PCU, bringing together over 50 participants. This was followed by a field visit by the Ricardo AEA team in Q3 2025, where further stakeholder consultations and data collection were undertaken for the Baseline Assessment. The findings of the Baseline Assessment are under review by the Ghana Maritime Authority and will be incorporated into the final draft NAP in early 2026, to be followed by formal adoption by the Government of Ghana.
Nigeria: Preparatory work for the development of Nigeria's NAP experienced some initial delays during the reporting period. To help advance the process and strengthen stakeholder understanding of the NAP approach, the GreenVoyage2050 PCU, together with the Government of Nigeria, organized a virtual introductory workshop in November 2025. The workshop brought together more than 40 stakeholders and provided an important opportunity to raise awareness of the NAP process, align expectations, and discuss Nigeria's role in developing and implementing a national maritime decarbonization strategy. The discussions helped build positive momentum for the process, and planning subsequently progressed for an in-person national stakeholder workshop scheduled for February 2026.

actual.value: The IMO VMDTF provides financial assistance to representatives of developing countries, in particular Small Island Developing States (SIDS) and Least Developed Countries (LDCs), to support their participation in IMO meetings on GHG related matters. The VMDTF is supported through donations from various Member States and international organizations. 2 In 2025, in order to enable the participation of representatives from SIDS and LDCs in IMO GHG-related meetings, the VMDTF was utilized to support attendance at the following four meetings: .1 the nineteenth meeting of the Intersessional Working Group on Reduction of GHG Emissions from Ships (ISWG-GHG 19); .2 the first meeting of the Intersessional Working Group on Air Pollution and Energy Efficiency (ISWG-APEE 1); .3 the 83rd session of the Marine Environment Protection Committee (MEPC 83); and .4 the second extraordinary meeting of MEPC (MEPC/ES.2) 3 To facilitate participation in these meetings, the VMDTF financed the attendance of 32 delegates from the following countries: Belize, Cambodia, Cook Islands, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Dominica, Egypt, Fiji, Gambia, Jamaica, Kenya, Madagascar, Marshall Islands, Mauritius, Mongolia, Namibia, Nauru, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Samoa, Senegal, Seychelles, Sierra Leone, Solomon Islands, Somalia, Suriname, Togo, Tonga, United Republic of Tanzania, Uganda, and Vanuatu. Due to the limited funds remaining in the VMDTF and the number of important GHG related meetings taking place in 2025, some of the unspent funds under outcomes 1 and 2, and anticipated funds for 2026 under outcome 3, for a total of US$ 195,000 were allocated to this output in support of the IMO VMDTF. 5 These transfers ensured the participation of delegates from SIDS and LDCs to IMO's GHG meetings in 2025. This contribution the VMDTF covered: .1 participants' travel costs; .2 daily subsistence allowance (DSA); .3 IMO support costs; and .4 UNDP support costs.

actual.value: The Workshop gathered more than 200 representatives from 35 African countries. The GHG TC Trust Fund facilitated attendance at the Workshop, through provision of travel and DSA funding, of 66 participants from 35 countries - Benin, Cabo Verde, Cameroon, Comoros, Congo, Cote d'Ivoire, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Djibouti, Egypt, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Morocco, Mozambique, Namibia, Nigeria, Sao Tome and Principe, Senegal, Seychelles, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Africa, South Sudan, Sudan, Togo, Uganda, United Republic of Tanzania and Zimbabwe. Delegates filled in a pre-workshop questionnaire and actively participated in breakout sessions. The main results from the questionnaire were summarized and presented. Participants shared experiences and identified areas for strengthened cooperation at the sub-regional level (North/East/West/Middle/Southern Africa). 3 The IMO Secretariat facilitated interactive group sessions focusing on: .1 increased ratification of MARPOL Annex VI; .2 National Action Plans on GHG reduction; .3 sustainable port development; .4 alternative fuel production and availability; .5 green maritime job creation and identification of green shipping investment opportunities; and .6 improved seafarer training. 4 The Workshop i contributed to increased awareness of the importance of shipping decarbonization and built towards: .1 increased ratification and implementation of MARPOL Annex VI in Africa; .2 enhanced national and sub-regional coordination; .3 strengthened collaboration between the maritime and energy sectors; .4 improved participation by African Member States at IMO Meetings; and .5 prioritization of seafarer training and green job opportunities. 5 A full report on the outcome of the Workshop was presented to the 75th session of IMO's Technical Cooperation Committee in document TC 75/INF.11 (Kenya). Workshop on promoting shipping decarbonization and the 43rd Annual Southern African Transport Conference (SATC), 9-10 July 2025, Pretoria, South Africa 1 Building on the outcomes of the Regional workshop on the implementation of the 2023 IMO GHG Strategy and Green Transition of Shipping in Africa, held in Mombasa, Kenya in February 2025, the South African Maritime Safety Authority (SAMSA) organized a one day workshop on promoting shipping decarbonization and aligning with the IMO Net-Zero Framework: Africa's Roles and Responsibilities, aimed at advancing the identified 'follow-up actions' in the Road Maps as well as deepening the understanding of the agreed IMO Net-Zero Framework. The workshop gathered 70 participants from public and private entities involved in the decarbonization of the South African maritime industry. IMO (through the GHG-TC Trust Fund) funded the participation of 9 participants from other African countries: Angola, Ghana, Kenya, Liberia and Namibia. In addition, the 43rd Southern African Transport Conference was held to explore effective provision of transport solutions under the broad theme of 'mobility solutions to southern African challenges', featuring a maritime session on maritime decarbonization. 3 The programme featured presentations and discussions on: .1 aligning with the IMO Net-Zero Framework; .2 decarbonization pathways: fuel transitions and technologies; .3 workforce development: capacity building for a green maritime future; .4 financing the net-zero transition: resource mobilization; and .5 relation / Impact on IMO. 4 The event was a direct follow-up from the Mombasa Workshop organized by IMO in February 2025. It will contribute to reinforcing awareness and coordination among African countries on the 2023 IMO GHG Strategy, including towards the adoption of the IMO Net-Zero Framework, and will help define national strategic priorities in that field. It also helped identify partners in the region to implement IMO initiatives. 5 The Workshop concluded with the identification of priority actions aligned with the Mombasa Roadmap presented during the 75th session of the IMO Technical Committee in June 2025, including concrete commitments to: .1 initiate or pursue the development of National Action Plans; .2 identify key decarbonization projects for investment, and consider the development of a feasibility assessment of alternative fuel production and supply capabilities and infrastructure needs; and .3 undertake skill gap assessment and modernize maritime education curricula for decarbonization. *** Regional workshop on 'Advancing Africa's maritime sector to net-zero', co-organized by the National Agency for Maritime Affairs of Senegal, the Professional African Technical and Advisory Initiative (PATNA) and the Maritime Organization of West and Central Africa (MOWCA), 4-6 August 2025, Dakar, Senegal 1 The purpose of this capacity building Workshop was to raise awareness on policies to reduce GHG emissions from ships, exchange views on how to ensure a just and equitable transition and gather African maritime authorities to build a common position ahead of the upcoming MEPC/ES.2 meeting, in the context of the expected adoption of the IMO Net-Zero Framework. 2 The Workshop brought together around 100 participants, both in person and online, primarily from African maritime administrations and entities, as well as representatives from the private sector involved in shipping decarbonization. It was hosted and organized by the National Agency for Maritime Affairs of Senegal, with support from the IMO Secretariat, which contributed a presentation and took part in a panel discussion. The programme featured presentations and a workshop panel divided into four parts: .1 Part I: scene setting to introduce and contextualize the workshop on the reduction of GHG emissions from ships; .2 Part II: scene setting to develop an African understanding of the meaning of just and equitable energy transition in the continental approach to reducing GHG emissions from ships; .3 Part III: scene setting on potential impact of the 2023 IMO GHG Strategy and the IMO Net-Zero Framework on Africa, SIDS and LDCs; and .4 Part IV: Scene setting to take a deep dive into the art of negotiating using evidence to support strategic African positions in global climate conversations with learnings from UNFCCC's African negotiators' experiences and relevant experts 4 A presentation was delivered on the IMO regulatory framework to address GHG emissions from ships, with a particular focus on the IMO Net-Zero Framework. Active engagement also took place with stakeholders regarding IMO technical assistance programmes and projects that support the ratification of MARPOL Annex VI, the implementation of GHG reduction measures, and participation in IMO meetings. 5 IMO provided technical expertise in the preparation of the Workshop programme. The event contributed to strengthening awareness and coordination among African countries on shipping decarbonization initiatives. It also helped identify potential partners in the region, particularly among Francophone African countries that have been less engaged in IMO discussions on GHG-related matters. 6 Senegal expressed its intention to ratify MARPOL Annex VI and its interest in requesting IMO technical assistance for the development of its Maritime Single Window and National Action Plan (NAP), as well as capacity-building support for its Port State Control Officers (PSCOs). 7 Participants expressed their appreciation for the VMDTF, which supports the participation of developing countries in IMO GHG-related meetings, and for the online core sessions of the GHG-SMART project. target.value: One situation assessment has been developed, identifying existing initiatives, gaps, challenges, and opportunities for improvements in knowledge sharing and coordination in Africa. One stakeholder mapping has been completed, identifying key stakeholders involved in the maritime sector in Africa. Stakeholders have been engaged through consultations, workshops, and meetings to understand their perspectives, priorities, and needs regarding knowledge-sharing and coordination.

One action plan for regional knowledge sharing and coordination has been developed, which includes identifying Priority Areas (such as technology adoption, regulatory compliance, capacity-building, data collection and analysis, and policy development) and creating actionable strategies. The action plan would involve engaging a wide range of stakeholders, including government agencies, industry representatives, academia, research institutions, and civil society organizations.

One regional conference has been held to promote the Regional Action Plan and share the latest research findings, best practices, case studies, and innovations related to GHG-reduction strategies and sustainable maritime practices. The conference should mark the start of the implementation of the Regional Action Plan
